Corollary 8.3
nodes.statement:
Suppose that the assumptions in Theorem 7.1 hold and let $ \mathcal{R}_{\beta,\chi}(q,N)$ be as defined there.
Assuming that $\beta_h$ is supported for $|h| \leq H$, we have
\begin{align*}
 & \mathcal{R}_{\beta,\chi}(q_1,q_2,N) \ll_\varepsilon  \,  Z^\varepsilon \bigg(\|\beta\|_1|H|^{2\vartheta_q}  \left(1+\bigg(\frac{CD}{q_2}\bigg)^{2\theta_q} \right)\left(1+ \mathrm{cond}(\chi)^{1/2}\bigg(\frac{N}{q}\bigg)^{1-2\theta_q}\right)  +\frac{\|\beta\|_1^2}{ N} \bigg), \\
   & \mathcal{R}_{h,\chi}(q_1,q_2,N) \ll_\varepsilon  \,   Z^\varepsilon \bigg(\|\beta\|_2^2 \left(1+\bigg(\frac{ H CD}{q_2}\bigg)^{2\theta_q} \right)\left(1+ \mathrm{cond}(\chi)^{1/2}\bigg(\frac{H N}{q}\bigg)^{1-2\theta_q}\right)   +\frac{\|\beta\|_1^2}{ N}\bigg), \\
 &\sum_{\substack{q=q_1q_2 \sim Q \\ q_1 \sim Q_1 \\ \mathrm{cond}(\chi) | q}}  \mathcal{R}_{h,\chi}(q_1,q_2,N) \ll_\varepsilon  \,  Z^\varepsilon \bigg(\|\beta\|_1|H|^{2\vartheta_q}   \bigg(\frac{Q} {\mathrm{cond}(\chi)}  + N + (CD Q_1 )^{2\theta} Q^{1-4\theta}\bigg) +     \frac{\|\beta\|_1^2 Q} { N\mathrm{cond}(\chi)} \bigg).
\end{align*}

nodes.name: Theorem 7.1
Theorem 1.1
Theorem 10.1
Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement:
Let $h,q\in {\mathbb Z}$ with $q$ square-free and $\gcd(h,q)=1$. Let $X,\eta > 0$ and suppose that $-X/2\leq h  \leq X^{1+\eta}$.  Let $G:{\mathbb R}\to{\mathbb C}$ be a smooth  function supported on $[1,2]$ that satisfies $G^{(j)} \ll_j X^{j \eta }$ for all $j \geq 0$. Let $t:{\mathbb Z}/q{\mathbb Z} \to {\mathbb C}$ be a function. Then for some binary quadratic polynomial $P_h$, only depending on $h$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \sum_{\substack{ n }} G(n/X) d(n) d(n+h)t(n) =&\sum_{r\,\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{q})} t(r)\omega(r,h;q) \int G(u/X)  P_h( \log u,\log(u+h)) \,\mathrm d u
        \\
        &\hspace{20pt}+O\bigg( X^{1/2+O(\eta)} q^{1/2}\|t\|_2   (|h|^{\theta}+(X/q)^{\theta})  \bigg),
    \end{align*}
where  $\|t\|_2^2 = \sum_{r \,\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{q})} |t(r)|^2$ and $\theta= 7/64$ denotes the best approximation to the Ramanujan-Peterson and Selberg eigenvalue conjectures.
